page: Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a dedicated server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with 2880 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and there are no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core stress-ng performance, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, and software compilation with Clang. Large-block memory bandwidth for both read and write operations also ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core stress-ng performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET operations fall into the strong (top 25%) category. For language model workloads, the instance achieves strong (top 25%) text generation speeds on small and medium models, though prompt processing on larger 70B models drops to average (middle 50%) performance.

The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores, high memory density, and substantial NVMe SSD storage offers a balanced resource profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. This configuration is suited for database operations, large-scale software compilation, text and image processing, and static web serving. The absence of hardware acceleration limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but it remains capable of CPU-based inference for smaller models.
